title: Multiwavelength and Multi-CO View of the Minor Merger Driven Star Formation in the Nearby LIRG NGC 3110
question: To better understand the physical properties of molecular gas, including the CO-to-H2 conversion factor (alpha_CO), and their relation to minor-merger-driven star formation in the nearby interacting LIRG NGC 3110.

data.arrays: 12 m array (29-41 antennas for Band 3, 35-38 antennas for Band 6)
data.angular_resolution: 1.16" x 1.14" to 1.81" x 1.43" native; convolved to 2.0"
data.sensitivity: 0.4 to 1.2 mJy beam^-1 per channel (20 or 40 km s^-1)

evidence.quote: In addition to the ALMA data, we use the H$\alpha$ map obtained with Okayama Astrophysical Observatory (OAO) 188 cm telescope. The observations and data reduction are described in detail in (cite: Hattori04).

what.value: VLT K-band map and super star cluster (SSC) candidate spatial distribution

evidence.quote: Furthermore, we use a high-quality $K$-band map obtained by Very Large Telescope (VLT) (see (cite: Randriamanakoto13) for details of the data), which provides the spatial distribution of SSCs.

what.value: Single-dish 12CO(1-0) total integrated flux measurement (395 +/- 79 Jy km s^-1)

evidence.quote: However, we caution that our $^{12}$CO($1\text{--}0$) data miss some extended emission (recovered flux $=$ 77 $\pm$ 15 %) compared to single dish measurement (395 $\pm$ 79 Jy km s$^{-1}$; (cite: Sanders91))

what.value: Upper state energies and Einstein coefficients for RADEX non-LTE modeling from Leiden Atomic and Molecular Database

evidence.quote: The upper state energies and the Einstein coefficients were taken from the *Leiden Atomic and Molecular Database* (cite: Schoier05).

what.value: Molecular transition parameters from Splatalogue and Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy

evidence.quote: We took the transition parameters necessary for calculating the equation from Splatalogue and the *Cologne Database for Molecular Spectroscopy* (cite: Muller01; Muller05).

recipe.goal: Calibrate and image ALMA line and continuum data and create moment maps
recipe.method: Flag anomalous visibility amplitudes, subtract continuum in uv domain, image lines and continuum with multiscale tclean using natural weighting, flag uv < 10 klambda for line ratio maps, correct primary beam, convolve to 2.0", and create masked moment maps.
key_parameters: uv range cutoff = 10 klambda for line ratios
assumptions: Flux calibration systematic errors of 5% (Band 3) and 10% (Band 6)

recipe.goal: Perform hexagonal Nyquist-sampled aperture photometry and compute line ratios
recipe.method: Extract integrated line intensities, brightness temperatures, luminosities, and line ratios across ALMA and ancillary maps using a hexagonal grid of 3.0" diameter apertures separated by 1.5", keeping data points > 3 sigma.
key_parameters: aperture diameter = 3.0", aperture separation = 1.5", SNR threshold = 3 sigma
assumptions: D_L = 69.4 Mpc; statistical and systematic errors are independent

recipe.goal: Model non-LTE molecular gas excitation using RADEX
recipe.method: Compare observed CO line ratios with non-LTE radiative transfer model grids generated by RADEX to derive gas kinetic temperature (T_kin) and H2 volume density (n_H2) at each aperture.
assumptions: Single-phase ISM, expanding sphere geometry with dv = 100 km s^-1, T_bg = 2.73 K, [CO]/[H2] = 3 x 10^-4, [CO]/[13CO] = 70

recipe.goal: Derive H2 gas masses and calibrate the CO-to-H2 conversion factor (alpha_CO)
recipe.method: Estimate H2 gas masses via two independent methods: (1) LTE calculation from optically-thin 13CO transitions assuming fixed T_rot = 15 K, and (2) Rayleigh-Jeans 1.3 mm dust continuum emission following Scoville et al. (2016). Compare both with L'_CO(1-0) to determine alpha_CO.
key_parameters: T_rot = T_d = 15 K; alpha_850 = 6.7 x 10^19 erg s^-1 Hz^-1 M_sun^-1; nu_obs = 235 GHz; adopted constant alpha_CO = 1.7 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1
assumptions: 13CO is optically thin in LTE; [13CO]/[H2] = 4.3 x 10^-6 ([12CO]/[13CO] = 70, [12CO]/[H2] = 3.0 x 10^-4); Helium factor = 1.36; T_d = T_rot = 15 K

recipe.goal: Compute millimeter spectral index, extinction-corrected SFR, SFE, and SSC surface density
recipe.method: Calculate millimeter spectral index between 1.3 mm and 2.9 mm continuum; compute extinction-corrected SFR from OAO H alpha and VLA 1.4 GHz continuum; compute Sigma_H2 (using untruncated 12CO(1-0) data and fixed alpha_CO = 1.7), SFE (= Sigma_SFR / Sigma_H2), and Sigma_SSC across apertures.
key_parameters: L(H_alpha)_corr = L(H_alpha)_obs + 0.39 x 10^13 L(1.4GHz); SFR = L(H_alpha)_corr / 10^41.27
assumptions: Global H alpha + 1.4 GHz extinction correction prescription holds for 3.0" (~1 kpc) apertures; fixed alpha_CO = 1.7 M_sun (K km s^-1 pc^2)^-1

evidence.quote: However, we caution that our $^{12}$CO($1\text{--}0$) data miss some extended emission (recovered flux $=$ 77 $\pm$ 15 %) compared to single dish measurement (395 $\pm$ 79 Jy km s$^{-1}$; (cite: Sanders91))
The $^{\rm 12}R_{21/10}$ shows a smooth distribution over the entire arms and bar-like elongation ($\sim$0.8 on average).

answer_key.quantity: 13R_21/10 line intensity ratio (center / ends of elongation / southern arm)

evidence.quote: The $^{\rm 13}R_{21/10}$ peaks at the center ($\sim$1.0) with lower values at the ends of the elongation ($\sim$0.7) and the southern arm ($\sim$0.4).
The median and average $T_{\rm rot}$ are 15.1 K and 15.4 K, respectively.
The derived 16$^{th}$–50$^{th}$–84$^{th}$ percentiles of $\alpha_{\rm LTE}$ ($=$ $M_{\rm LTE}$/$L'_{\rm CO(1-0)}$) are 1.30–1.69–2.21 $M_{\odot}$ (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$)$^{-1}$.
The derived 16$^{th}$–50$^{th}$–84$^{th}$ percentiles of $\alpha_{\rm ISM}$ are 1.08–1.48–2.26 $M_{\odot}$ (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$)$^{-1}$.

answer_key.quantity: Best-fit Gaussian peak of alpha_ISM(T_rot) and adopted typical alpha_CO

evidence.quote: Figure 7 (right) shows the histogram of $\alpha_{\rm ISM}$($T_{\rm rot}$) with a best-fit Gaussian (peak $=$ 1.73 and dispersion $=$ 0.48). In this paper, we adopt a fixed $\alpha_{\rm CO}$ of 1.7 $M_{\odot}$ (K km s$^{-1}$ pc$^2$)$^{-1}$
The derived total SFR from the extinction-corrected H$\alpha$ data (i.e., summed over all independent apertures) is $\sim$18 $M_{\odot}$ yr$^{-1}$(Figure 6 middle-left).

score_reason: ALMA project code, calibration/imaging software (CASA 4.2.2), weighting, smoothing beam, uv-clipping, aperture sizes, and all analytic formulas for LTE mass, ISM mass, RADEX grid bounds, and SFR are explicitly written out. However, custom manual flagging details, tclean deconvolution parameters, and external OAO/VLT maps are not directly provided.
rediscovery_reason: The ALMA Cycle 2 dataset (2013.1.01172.S) is public, and the core ALMA-only numeric results—integrated line fluxes for 5 CO isotopologue transitions, line ratios, T_rot, alpha_LTE, alpha_ISM, and millimeter spectral indices—are derived via explicitly stated equations on 2.0" convolved maps.
